title: -ing and infinitive
subtitle: Verbs followed by -ing, the full infinitive, or both

blocks.text: Some verbs are sometimes followed by **-ing**: He enjoys **making** other people laugh.

items: After a preposition, we usually use **-ing**. I'm afraid **of flying**.

blocks.text: Some phrases end in the preposition **to**. These are also followed by **-ing**, not an infinitive.

blocks.correct: I look forward **to hearing** from you.
blocks.incorrect: I look forward **to hear** from you.

items: We can also use the **-ing** form as the subject of a sentence. **Cooking** is great fun!

blocks.text: Some verbs are sometimes followed by the full infinitive: I decided **to apologise** to Emma.

blocks.intro: Some verbs are followed by an object + bare infinitive (without **to**).
items: Don't **let** the dog **sit** on the sofa.

blocks.text: **Make** in the passive is followed by the full infinitive.

blocks.correct: Michael **was made to apologise** by his mother.
blocks.incorrect: Michael **was made apologise** by his mother.

items: Some verbs are followed by the full infinitive alone and some can be followed by an object + full infinitive.
He **wants me to tell** him a joke.

blocks.text: Some verbs can be followed by either **-ing** or the full infinitive. I started **liking / to like** James after he helped me with my problem.

blocks.intro: With these verbs, the meaning is the same or nearly the same:

rows.example: have a memory in your mind — Do you **remember seeing** that comedy?
do something you are/were planning to do — Did you **remember to say** sorry to James?
not be able to remember a past event — I'd **forgotten hearing** that joke.
not do something you are/were planning to do — Oh, no! I **forgot to invite** Shelly!
stop an action — **Stop crying** — it's not that bad.
interrupt an action to do something else — I was on my way to see Maria and I **stopped to get** her some flowers.
do something to try and solve a problem — Have you **tried talking** to her?
make an effort to do something — I'm **trying to say** I'm sorry, but you won't listen!

exercises.title: D · Similar meaning
exercises.instruction: Complete each second sentence using the word given, so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence. Write between two and five words.

items.prompt:
They finally succeeded in escaping from the room. **managed**
They finally ___ from the room.
acceptedAnswers: They finally managed to escape from the room.
They finally managed to escape from the room

items.prompt:
I bought a new notebook on the way to school. **stopped**
On the way to school, I ___ a new notebook.
acceptedAnswers: On the way to school, I stopped to buy a new notebook.
